12.1a — Grid/Symmetry Jam: Kickoff & Pitch

The exam is behind you. The games are not. Third jam, and the constraint is structural this time: a GRID with SYMMETRY — the design language of Tetris, Picross, chess, Snake, Minesweeper. When the grid is the rule, every design decision multiplies.

Kickoff ~15 min

What the constraint means:

  • Grid: movement, placement, or both snap to cells — think in indices, not coordinates (your 7.1a tilemap was a grid you PAINTED; this one you PROGRAM)
  • Symmetry: the game state, the board, or the CONTROLS mirror somehow — vertical (chess: both sides same), rotational (Tetris: each piece is its own mirror), or player-vs-player (both play identical rules)
  • Either half may dominate: a grid game with light symmetry, or a symmetric duel on a grid

You have already done grid math without noticing: your hand of cards rendered by index (10.2c — position = index × spacing). A grid is that, in two axes: x = column * cellSize. The symmetry half? Your turret personalities (3.4a) were mirrored difficulty — same idea, one axis up.

Socratic

Symmetry is a GENERATOR: define one half, mirror it, get the second half free. Where in code does that save work (spawn positions? level halves? an AI that plays YOUR OWN rules — like your card AI (10.2d) but as player two)? Which symmetry would make your game's content FREE?

Pitch & Vote ~30 min

Pitch card (10 min):

  1. One sentence: "a grid game where ___ is symmetric because ___"
  2. The core loop: one move, its consequence, why it repeats
  3. The symmetry's JOB: fairness (duel)? difficulty (mirror match)? beauty (pattern play)? — name it
  4. Reused-parts list (10.1a rules: honest inventory)

30-second pitches → votes → teams of 1–3 (same contracts as every jam). This is the last new-team formation of the year: choose for who you work WELL with, not who you sit near.

Bug Hunt: Pitch-time scope checks

  1. A pitch with BOTH real-time action AND grid logic. Which half dies first under deadline — and what does "turn-based or nothing" buy the last jam of the year?
  2. Symmetry of RULES but not of BOARD (chess has both). Which one can you BUILD in two classes — and which is just an if-statement?

Tinker: Tonight

  1. Jam README with the pitch card + the INPUT table (10.1a format). What does "press W" MEAN on a grid (column, row, +/−1) — write the mapping now.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Name three real grid games and their symmetry type
  • Pitch a grid+symmetry loop in one sentence
  • Define the input → grid mapping in your README
